brief: Rabobank expects the FOMC to hold at 3.75-4.00% on October 27-28, but not unanimously: Hammack, Kashkari and Logan are expected to repeat their July hike dissents, since September's dot plot carried four dots implying two more 25bp hikes before year-end, three of which belong to actual voters (the July dissenters), and recent inflation data have likely strengthened that camp. Skipping October lets the Fed see more data and still reach its year-end target via a December hike, while also avoiding a hike a week before the midterms, which the FOMC will publicly deny factored in; Trump has separately said he wants lower rates. At the press conference, Warsh is expected to repeat Jackson Hole's hawkish no-forward-guidance stance: he may say inflation trends have not meaningfully improved without saying a hike is imminent. Rabobank expects the December hike, helped by oil-driven CPI pressure, then a hold through 2027 (risk skewed higher on further inflation) before cutting starting Q1 2028 (pencilled March), then March 2029 and March 2030, to a 3.25-3.50% terminal range, less easing than the Fed's own 3.2% longer-run dot.
